summary: Powell County cabin on Lolo NF: firelookout.com dates it to 1929 though a 1928 newspaper already describes it; gone by 1958; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: cabin, with a crow's nest about 2 miles southeast atop Conger Point (firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: Gone 1958 per firelookout.com; the Montana page says removed; no source describes the site today

events.note: July 28, 1928 Daily Missoulian item, quoted on montanalookouts, already describes the Fenn Mountain lookout as able to spot fires and plans a telephone line to its top
cabin, per firelookout.com; this date comes after the 1928 newspaper mention
'Gone 1958' per firelookout.com; the page does not say how it was removed

evidence.supports: location: about 17 miles east of Seeley Lake
built 1929 as a cabin; gone 1958; crow's nest 2 miles southeast atop Conger Point
evidence.quote: 1929: cabin. Gone 1958. Also a crows nest 2 miles southeast atop Conger Point.

evidence.supports: 1928 item describes the lookout as capable of spotting fires; elevation 8,200
evidence.quote: The Fenn mountain lookout, situated at an 8,200 elevation, is capable of spotting fires in that district

evidence.supports: the 1928 item is from The Daily Missoulian
planned telephone line from Monture to the top of the mountain
evidence.quote: A new standard telephone line, extending from Monture to the top of Fenn mountain, will be constructed soon

evidence.supports: reason for the line, in part: upper Swan River area was as yet unprotected by lines of communication
evidence.quote: The necessity of the new line is brought about partly by the fact that the upper Swan river area is as yet unprotected by lines of communication.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com dates the cabin to 1929, but a July 1928 Daily Missoulian item, quoted on montanalookouts, already describes the lookout; the story keeps both and does not reconcile them
firelookout.com gives 8241 feet; the 1928 item gives 8,200; the story gives both figures

notes_for_editor: Gone status is consistent across three sources. The build year (1929) conflicts with a 1928 newspaper item, and the elevation differs slightly (8241 vs 8,200). Only three thin pages were available; no Lolo National Forest record or newspaper archive was reached. Records place the site at 47.21725, -113.12463.
